title: 西醫新法([1872];Bodleian Sinica 1826) / Xi yi xin fa [New methods of Western medicine]: Transcription dataset
description:
《西醫新法》（Xi yi xin fa）是討論外科與包紮的晚清漢譯醫學文獻，署嘉約翰（John Glasgow Kerr）口譯、林湘東筆述；Bodleian Sinica 1826 的館目供定刊地 [Canton]、年代 [1872]。本資料集依25幅影像提供44個指定物理面的 TXT、JSON、TEI XML、疑讀與來源對應，可供晚清醫學翻譯、包紮史及圖文關係研究。文字為 AI 暫定轉錄並經局部原圖修訂，未經人類全文雙校或專家審定。

Xi yi xin fa [New methods of Western medicine] is a late-Qing Chinese work on surgery and bandaging, credited to John Glasgow Kerr for oral translation and Lin Xiangdong for written rendering. The catalogue for Bodleian Sinica 1826 supplies [Canton] and [1872]. Based on 25 images, the dataset provides TXT, JSON and TEI XML for 44 designated physical faces, with uncertainties and source mappings for research on medical translation, bandaging history and image-text relationships. The provisional AI transcription includes selected source-image corrections; full human double collation and expert review have not been performed.

Scope: 25 fixed images / 44 designated physical faces. Literary Chinese text with English documentation. Historical text and faithful mechanical transcription receive no new exclusive restriction; copyrightable original documentation and arrangement are CC BY 4.0. Source scans/crops are excluded and retain the separate Bodleian terms in RIGHTS.md and LICENSE.md, including CC BY-NC 4.0 where recorded. Bracketed English titles are editorial translations. Prior v0.2.0 DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23971701; this proposed v0.2.1 DOI is unknown and omitted.

# Methods / 處理方法

v0.2.1 applies a targeted, nonblind review of 9 selected reader questions against the same fixed Bodleian images. Proposed readings and their rationale were already known before image review. Full parent frames were viewed together with original-pixel details where needed. 12 individually specified literal operations (12 codepoints) are adopted; retained and unresolved proposals are listed with source references in TARGETED-CORRECTIONS.json. This round is not a fresh whole-book independent collation.



The previous v0.2.0 whole-book AI observation, comparison and source-adjudication history remains preserved in HISTORICAL-METHODS-v0.2.0.md and the existing JSON history. Its coverage and failed or incomplete activities are not upgraded by this selected review. Historical count statements describe that version; current counts are 472 units, 9189 literal Unicode codepoints and 71 active uncertainty declarations. Codepoint counts include reference strings where present and are not source character counts or error rates.

No Unicode normalization, global variant or punctuation replacement, reading-order change, gaiji-ID change, or modernization is applied. Fixed unit strings drive the JSON, TXT and TEI XML exports without new model rewriting. Unknown glyph extent remains unknown; original uncertainties and superseded readings remain in version history. The two current gaiji reference notations, where present, remain unchanged.

Full human double collation, expert review, peer review and accuracy measurement have not been performed. Exact model identifiers, reasoning settings and complete token counters for the native AI review were not reported and remain unknown. Format, schema, hash and round-trip checks establish engineering properties only. The minimal TEI P5 projection is not a complete scholarly apparatus; no custom ODD or Schematron is claimed.

Source scans and crops, dedicated programs, prompts and complete private working records are excluded. The complete image-to-text production method is not publicly reproducible from this package. See RIGHTS.md and LICENSE.md for the distinct historical-text, original-documentation and Bodleian-image terms. This is historical-document transcription; no biological research or modern clinical instructions are provided.
